demand.question: What is Amazon Aurora, and which two database engines is it compatible with (MySQL and PostgreSQL)? Is it a fully managed relational database engine?

What throughput does AWS claim for Aurora compared with standard MySQL and standard PostgreSQL on the same hardware (the 'up to five times' and 'up to three times' claims)? Quote the exact wording and where it appears.
demand.note: numbers: current pages say up to 6x for both engines; no saved page states a three times PostgreSQL figure. adjudicate-27: the decision-guide five-times fact was rejected as older wording (currency unsure).

demand.question: What is an Aurora DB cluster: one or more DB instances plus a cluster volume? Which instance is the primary (writer) and what do Aurora Replicas (readers) do?
How many Aurora Replicas can one Aurora DB cluster have in addition to the primary instance (15)?
Does the primary instance handle both reads and writes, and are Aurora Replicas read-only? Which instance runs DDL and DML statements?
Do all instances of a cluster share one cluster volume, so that Aurora Replicas read the same data without copying it? How does this separate compute from storage?
Across how many Availability Zones does Aurora store copies of the cluster volume data, and how many copies (six copies across three AZs)? Is this true even for a cluster with a single DB instance?
What is the maximum size of an Aurora cluster volume (128 TiB, or 256 TiB on newer engine versions)? Which engine versions get the larger limit?
demand.note: numbers: 256 TiB is quoted; the engine versions that allow 256 TiB are bullet lines on CHAP_Limits without a quotable sentence

demand.question: Hypothesis (FRESHNESS): the Aurora storage maximum rose from 128 TiB to 256 TiB in July 2025 for supported versions. Confirm the date, old value and new value on an AWS page.
Does the cluster volume grow automatically as data grows, so that you never provision storage size? Does it shrink when data is removed (dynamic resizing)?
How is Aurora storage reliable: is it fault tolerant and self-healing, with data in segments that are repaired automatically? What does the guide say about losing an AZ?
How does Aurora recover after a crash (no replay of the redo log at startup; fast crash recovery)? Does the buffer cache survive a restart (survivable page cache)?
Where does an Aurora cluster run: in one AWS Region, across Availability Zones of that Region? What must the DB subnet group contain (subnets in at least two AZs)?

Which DB instance class families does Aurora offer (memory optimized db.r*, burstable db.t* for dev and test, Graviton classes, db.serverless)? What does the guide say about burstable classes for production?
FAQ: Does Aurora require special drivers, or do existing MySQL and PostgreSQL drivers and tools work unchanged?
What does the cluster endpoint (writer endpoint) connect to, and does it follow the new primary after a failover without an application change?
What does the reader endpoint do: load-balance read-only connections across the Aurora Replicas? Where does it connect when the cluster has no replica (to the primary)?
Does the reader endpoint balance connections, not individual queries? What does that mean for long-lived connection pools?
What is an instance endpoint, and when should an application use one instead of the cluster or reader endpoint?
What is a custom endpoint (a group of chosen instances, for example larger replicas for analytics or reporting)? How does it differ from the reader endpoint?
How many custom endpoints can one Aurora cluster have? Any other quota on endpoints?
Which endpoint types does the guide recommend for high availability (cluster endpoint for writes, reader endpoint for reads), and why should applications avoid hard-coding instance endpoints?
What replica lag does Aurora state for Aurora Replicas (typically well under 100 milliseconds after the primary writes)?
